newsitem.title: USA: Three dead as small plane crashes off NY beach.
newsitem.headline: Three dead as small plane crashes off NY beach.

text.p: A single-engine plane crashed in water off New York's popular Jones Beach on Tuesday, killing three people on board, authorities said.

The plane had emerged from fog and crashed into Jones Beach Inlet, said Nassau County police officer Adele Burke. Witnesses said the plane appeared to be struggling to gain altitude but failed and plunged into the water, she said.

The body of a woman was found in the water and the bodies of a man and a woman were found in the plane, she said. Because of strong currents, police divers could not recover the plane, which was submerged in 30 feet of water, until morning, she said. A boat was to stay with the wreckage.
The plane was a Grummond Tiger that had just taken off from Republic Airport in Farmingdale, N.Y., on Long Island, and was headed to Lancaster, Pa., a Federal Aviation Administration spokesman said.
Initial information about the 2 p.m. crash indicated three bodies were found. Burke later changed the information, bringing the body count down to one.

At first the police marine aviation unit located two of the bodies with sonar, she said. That unconfirmed report should not have been released, she said. Later, divers located the bodies in the stranded wreckage and confirmed that a man and a woman died in the plane in addition to a woman whose body was found in the water, she said.
The victims were not identified. The cause of the crash was under investigation.
Jones Beach State Park is located about 25 miles from Midtown Manhattan.
